heroHeadline: GSF Full Operations Launch June 1; MSF Hospital Day 22 Closure; 1.5M Displaced — HRP Only 23% Funded
heroSubtitle: On May 31, 2026 — the eve of the Gang Suppression Force's scheduled full operations launch — Haiti's acute humanitarian emergency shows no near-term relief. MSF's Cité Soleil hospital enters its 22nd consecutive day of forced closure, its longest documented uninterrupted shutdown since the 2021 crisis began, leaving approximately 300,000 commune residents without emergency medical access. The GSF's advance force of approximately 800 personnel — representing less than 15% of the 5,500-person authorized ceiling under UNSCR 2793 — is exclusively concentrated in Port-au-Prince's city center with no coverage for Cité Soleil, Martissant, or the Artibonite. The 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan remains only approximately 23% funded ($198.7M of $880M secured), with 6.4 million Haitians in acute food insecurity including 600,000+ in IPC Phase 5 (Catastrophe/near-famine). On May 30, Haitian women's organizations used the occasion of Haitian Mother's Day to publicly demand protection for gang violence victims — highlighting that women and children constitute more than half of the 1.5 million internally displaced persons confirmed by the UN on May 29. In a rare moment of national unity on May 29–30, Haiti's football team qualified for the World Cup for the first time in over 50 years, triggering street celebrations in Port-au-Prince even as the team trains in Florida and New Jersey because gang control of 75–90% of the capital makes home training impossible. The US Supreme Court ruling on TPS for approximately 350,000 Haitian nationals remains expected in late June–early July 2026, with the Court's conservative majority appearing to lean toward upholding the Trump administration's termination authority during oral arguments.
